key_insight: 2D/3D perovskite band alignment is highly sensitive to surface termination and chemical composition, which strongly shifts work function and band offsets at the interface.
engineering_relevance: Careful interface engineering of 2D passivation layers on 3D perovskites can improve solar-cell performance and stability by tuning electronic alignment and interfacial polarization.
method: Consistent calculation of work function, electron affinity, and band offsets
evidence_signal: The abstract reports preliminary computed results showing work functions and band offsets vary substantially with cleavage, termination, and ionic substitution, with valence offsets of 0.2–0.7 eV and conduction offsets around 0.25 eV.
watch_item: Results are preliminary and computational; real device performance may differ because interface disorder, defects, and fabrication conditions are not yet fully included.
paper_title: Material chemical composition impacts on the band alignments: preliminary results on the 3D/2D perovskite interfaces
